issue.title: Codex 经 magpie 网关时每次会话先尝试 WebSocket 被 426 拒、再回退 HTTP——每会话一条 ERROR 日志与启动延迟
issue.body:
## 环境
- macOS 26 (arm64)，magpie 源码构建（commit `a93190a`，2026-10-24）
- codex-cli 0.164.0
- provider：`zai`（preset 一条命令接入），模型 `zai/glm-5.3`
- 网关 headless：`magpie web --gateway --no-open`（gateway 127.0.0.1:3425）
## 复现（3 步）
1. `magpie web --gateway --no-open`（或任意方式起网关）
2. `magpie codex zai/glm-5.3`
3. `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only "回复OK"` （任意 prompt 均可）
## 实际行为
每个会话启动都会先对网关发起 WebSocket 连接并被拒，打一条 ERROR 后回退 HTTP，请求本身成功：
```
2026-10-23T20:14:30.060503Z ERROR codex_api::endpoint::responses_websocket: failed to connect to websocket: HTTP error: 426 Upgrade Required, url: ws://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex/responses
```
magpie 写入 Codex 配置的路由是内置 openai provider + `openai_base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex"`（同时移除了原有的 `model_provider` 行）。Codex 对这条 backend-api 路径默认先试 WebSocket。
## 期望行为
会话启动不走注定失败的 WebSocket 尝试：无 ERROR 日志、无回退延迟。
## 对照（同机同版本）
自定义 provider 显式声明不支持 WebSocket 时完全干净——直接 HTTP、无任何 WS 日志：
```toml
[model_providers.oahttp]
# …
supports_websockets = false
```
同一条 `codex exec` 命令在 oahttp provider 下无 ERROR、正常回包。
## 观察
`internal/agent/codex.go` 的 `codexReachedRead` 会从 Codex 日志里挖 `connecting to websocket:` 行作为"已到达网关"的证据，说明 426 回退是 magpie 预期内的行为；但对用户侧这是每次会话一条的 ERROR，观感像故障（我一开始也当成 magpie 的 bug 报了）。
## 建议（供参考）
Codex 0.162.1 起不允许覆盖内置 openai provider 的传输配置，所以 `supports_websockets=false` 没法直接加在内置 provider 上。可否评估：
1. 路由改走已写入的 `[model_providers.magpie]` 自定义表（`wire_api = "responses"` + `supports_websockets = false` + `model_provider = "magpie"`），从源头跳过 WS 尝试；或
2. 网关对 `/backend-api/codex/responses` 的 WS 升级请求返回更友好的信号 / 在文档里说明这条 ERROR 属预期回退。
## 附：magpie 对 ~/.codex/config.toml 的完整改动（diff 摘要，仅背景）
> 本 issue 只报 WebSocket 一件事；`codex default` 的还原残留（`enabled-reasoning-efforts`、`[model_providers.magpie]` 死块）是另一个问题，会单独报。
```diff
-model_provider = "oahttp"        # 原默认 provider 行被移除
 model = "zai/glm-5.3"            # 原 gpt-6.1-sol
+openai_base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/backend-api/codex"
+enabled-reasoning-efforts = ["low","medium","high","xhigh","ultra","persistent","max"]
+[model_providers.magpie]
+name = "magpie"
+base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1"
+wire_api = "responses"
+experimental_bearer_token = "magpie"
+http_headers = { "x-openai-actor-authorization" = "magpie" }
```

comments.body:
跟进核对：当前上游已经通过支持 WebSocket 处理了原帖中网关返回 426 的原因，不需要再把 Codex 切到自定义 provider。

上游提交 ffa07395eb274cbe6cea299d825bf4f5c58db6e2（#4058）：https://github.com/yetone/magpie/commit/ffa07395eb274cbe6cea299d825bf4f5c58db6e2 。该提交已包含在本轮核对的 main b1e8eb15 中，原帖使用的 /backend-api/codex/responses 路径现在接受 WebSocket，并支持后续轮次的 delta。

我重新运行了该固定版本的五项离线网关测试：TestCodexSocketServed、TestCodexSocketLiteTurnLeavesLiteForARelay、TestResponsesSocketGuards、TestResponsesSocketContinues、TestCodexSocketOtherPaths，全部通过。覆盖模拟外部模型、ChatGPT 认证头保留、连续两轮对话和访问保护。

补充纠正历史 fork 分支的范围：0ffac708 仅关闭自定义/CC Switch provider 表中的 WebSocket，并没有解决原帖的内置 OpenAI 路径；现在应以这次上游 WebSocket 实现为准，无需叠加那份旧补丁。

未验证原帖的 macOS/Codex 0.164/真实 zai 账号，也没有启动已登录 Codex。若升级后仍看到 426，还需检查实际运行的二进制及反向代理是否允许 WebSocket upgrade；上述离线结果不代表这些部署条件已经验证。

跟进确认（2026-11-10）：升级后已实测，修复有效。

- magpie：源码 main `b922e516`（含 #4058 的 ffa0739）
- 环境：macOS 26 (arm64)、codex-cli 0.167.0、provider `zai`（真实上游 glm-5.3）、网关 `magpie web --gateway --no-open`
- 按原帖步骤 `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only`：Responses WebSocket 握手直接 **101** 成功，全程走 WS，**无 426、无 HTTP 回退、无 ERROR 日志**，回复正常返回：

```
INFO responses_websocket: connecting to Responses WebSocket
INFO responses_websocket: successfully connected to Responses WebSocket status=101
```

补上了 @skygunner 未验证的真实 macOS + 真实 zai 上游场景。问题已解决，关闭本 issue。

issue.title: feat(codex): 支持 Responses WebSocket 持续连接与增量续接

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### 诉求

希望 Magpie 支持 Codex 客户端的 Responses WebSocket 接入，并在多轮工具调用中保留持续连接和增量续接能力，降低重复建连和传输完整上下文的开销。

日常使用场景是 Codex 经本机 Magpie 进行连续读文件、修改代码、运行命令等长任务，希望保留 Magpie 的账号管理能力，同时尽量接近 Codex 直连的传输效率。

### 已核对的当前实现

本机使用 Magpie 0.1.1805；另外核对了上游源码提交 [`4655e165`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/commit/4655e16599046c02679a1477afece01d51eae686)。目前需要区分两个方向：

- **Codex → Magpie**：[`codexBackend`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/4655e16599046c02679a1477afece01d51eae686/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go#L64-L69) 对 WebSocket Upgrade 明确返回 426，要求客户端回退 HTTP；[`/v1/responses`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/4655e16599046c02679a1477afece01d51eae686/internal/gateway/gateway.go#L826-L838) 也有相同限制。
- **Magpie → ChatGPT 上游**：已经有 [`codexSocket`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/4655e16599046c02679a1477afece01d51eae686/internal/gateway/codex_socket.go#L24-L54) 支持流式请求走 WebSocket，再转换为 SSE 返回客户端。但源码明确说明当前是每轮新建 socket、发送完整请求体，没有保留 Codex 原生的持续连接与 `previous_response_id` 增量发送方式。

因此，这个请求是补齐客户端 WebSocket 和跨轮连接复用，而不是认为 Magpie 完全没有 WebSocket 实现。

### 期望行为

1. 在上游支持且不冲突于现有账号、权限与路由策略时，允许 Codex 通过 `/backend-api/codex/responses` 建立 Responses WebSocket。
2. 在同一响应链中复用上游连接，支持 `response.create`、`previous_response_id` 和增量输入，减少每轮重复握手及完整上下文上传。
3. 保留正确的取消、用量记录和错误语义；不支持或无法继续当前连接时，提供明确的 HTTP/SSE 回退或重新建立上下文的恢复方式，避免切换账号后丢失响应链。

实现后建议在同账号、同模型、同任务条件下，对比直连、当前 HTTP/SSE 接入和持续 WebSocket 接入的首段输出延迟、多轮工具调用总耗时及传输字节数。

[OpenAI WebSocket mode 文档](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/websocket-mode)说明了持续连接与增量输入对多轮工作流的用途。这里提出的是减少传输开销的方向，尚未完成受控 A/B 测试，不主张已经证明具体提速比例，也不把模型推理时间归因于代理。

### 相关讨论

- #3231：端到端 WebSocket 接入与转发。
- #2472：单账号原生 WebSocket 的 fork 实现与验证范围。
- #3449：客户端握手被 426 拒绝后回退 HTTP。

已看到这些讨论。本 issue 补充持续连接、增量续接和可对照验证的延迟诉求；如更适合合并到现有跟踪项，也可以按重复项处理。

issue.title: gateway: record the actual Codex upstream transport and WebSocket fallback reason

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Problem

With three Codex subscription accounts configured in Magpie v0.1.2131, I cannot determine whether a particular upstream attempt used WebSocket or fell back to HTTP. This matters when checking whether WebSocket is working through the local proxy and diagnosing long streamed requests.

This is a request for transport observability, not a report that a WebSocket handshake actually failed.

## Observed environment and evidence

- Magpie desktop v0.1.2131, macOS 27.0.1 arm64.
- Codex subscription requests use the `/backend-api/codex/responses` route.
- After the update, local `usage.jsonl` records contained requests from all three accounts, but no transport, handshake, or fallback-result field.
- The running desktop process had standard error directed to `/dev/null`. Searching the retained system logs did not recover a Magpie-specific WebSocket fallback message.

To observe the gap, make an ordinary streamed Codex request through Magpie and inspect its corresponding usage record. The record does not establish which upstream transport was used. A final HTTP 200 does not prove that the upstream used WebSocket; 499 or 502 alone does not establish a handshake failure either.

No live handshake failure was deliberately triggered, no upstream 101 response was captured, and no fake-upstream regression test was run for this report. The evidence above is local record inspection plus source inspection.

## Source inspection

The relevant implementation in v0.1.2131 is:

- [upstreamTransport](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2131/internal/gateway/upstream_transport.go#L30) installs the Codex WebSocket transport.
- [codexSocket.RoundTrip](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2131/internal/gateway/codex_socket.go#L141) selects WebSocket or the HTTP path, including the temporary host and message-size bypasses.
- [socket](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2131/internal/gateway/codex_socket.go#L273) handles handshake failure and falls back to HTTP.
- [shunCodexSocket](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2131/internal/gateway/codex_socket.go#L127) logs some failures and temporarily bypasses WebSocket by host. Other early-close and connection-limit fallbacks have separate branches.
- [usage.Record](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.2131/internal/usage/usage.go#L29) records account, route, status, timing and errors, but no actual upstream transport result.

The same WebSocket source blob is present on main at `d80d75f300274fe13866d4fbf5599c13870b43ac`, checked on 2026-10-30.

## Requested behavior

Please expose the actual upstream transport in the existing request details or Routing trace, with a persisted local record so it remains inspectable after the request ends.

1. Record whether each upstream attempt used WebSocket, used HTTP directly, or fell back from WebSocket to HTTP.
2. When fallback or bypass occurs, distinguish the observed reason: handshake rejection/timeout, temporary host bypass, message-too-large handling, upstream connection limit, or an early socket close.
3. Correlate that result with the existing request/attempt and selected account. Host-wide fallback can affect several accounts, so a process-level message alone cannot answer which requests used it.
4. Keep handshake success, transport choice and response completion separate. A successful handshake is not proof of a completed response. Preserve the actual final status and existing errors.
5. Keep old or unobserved transport values unknown. Do not infer upstream WebSocket from the client transport, endpoint, configuration or a successful HTTP status.

The exact schema and presentation are up to the maintainers; this can fit the existing usage/trace path. Record only the diagnostic metadata needed, without prompts, response bodies, credentials, or raw authentication headers.

## Suggested validation, not performed

Use a fake upstream to compare successful WebSocket delivery, rejected/timed-out handshakes with HTTP fallback, temporary host bypass, close status 1009, connection-limit errors, and a socket closing before the response starts. Check ordinary HTTP and legacy records too.

Assert the persisted transport and fallback reason, correlated with the request/attempt and account. Include a late stream failure to ensure handshake success is not mislabeled as response completion. These are proposed acceptance checks, not claims of completed testing.

## Related scope

- #2472 includes dual-leg transport display in a larger single-account native WebSocket proposal/fork. This issue isolates observability of the already-shipped upstream path, including multiple saved accounts and HTTP fallback.
- #4058 tracks client-side persistent Responses WebSocket and delta continuation; its shipped client connection does not establish the upstream transport.
- #3948 covers protocol-error/client-error observability. This request concerns transport selection and fallback reasons.

This does not request changes to routing, retries, account switching, connection pooling or transport policy.

issue.title: provider: let a custom Responses provider (a Codex relay such as Krill AI) take its turns over the relay's WebSocket

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What I have

- magpie `0.1.3352`, macOS, pi as the agent.
- A custom provider for a Codex relay, already working over HTTP:

  ```
  id         krill-ai-codex
  responses  https://api.kbsfdxc.net/codex/v1
  models     gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-astra
  ```

pi talks to magpie over loopback (`/v1/responses`) and should keep doing so. The leg I want on a different transport is magpie → relay.

## The relay serves the same turn over a WebSocket, which is also the faster path there

Krill AI's own docs (Chinese) tell Pi/Codex users to enable it: one socket per session, each turn a frame, `previous_response_id` for the next one. I probed the endpoint directly (Node `ws`, current key, `api.kbsfdxc.net`, model `gpt-6.1-sol`):

```
GET wss://api.kbsfdxc.net/codex/v1/responses
Authorization: Bearer <key>
OpenAI-Beta: responses_websockets=2026-02-06
```

| probe | result |
| --- | --- |
| handshake | `101`, 230–270 ms; the `OpenAI-Beta` header is *not* enforced by this relay (101 with or without it) |
| one turn | frame `{"type":"response.create", …whole Responses body…}` → 10–17 frames back, one per SSE event (`response.created` … `response.completed`), first `response.output_text.delta` 2.2–2.5 s |
| after `response.completed` | socket stays `OPEN` (no per-turn reconnect) |
| turn 2 as a delta | frame with only the new `input` + `previous_response_id` → correct contextual answer, `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens: 3968` |
| `service_tier: "priority"` | accepted (the relay's "Fast") |
| magpie-shaped body | `client_metadata`, `prompt_cache_key`, `reasoning.effort`, `store:false`, `text.verbosity`, `include:["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` all accepted |
| 100 s idle on a kept socket | still `OPEN`, the next `previous_response_id` turn answers |
| `User-Agent`/`originator: codex_cli_rs` | not required |
| a third line, `api-slb.kbsfdxc.net` (国内线路) | TLS reset from here, so all probes are `api.kbsfdxc.net` |

The same turn over HTTP, on the same key and model, for scale: `POST …/codex/v1/responses` took 3.04 s to the first byte (headers at 3044 ms, first event 3045 ms, `response.completed` 3085 ms), where the socket had its handshake at 265 ms and the first `output_text.delta` at 2.2–2.5 s. So the socket is at least as fast on this line; what it buys beyond that is the kept connection and a delta turn, not a one-off latency win.

So the relay speaks exactly what `internal/gateway/codex_socket.go` already sends to `chatgpt.com`: the HTTP body with `"type":"response.create"` ahead of it, events back as frames, and a socket that outlives a turn.

## Why I think this belongs in core rather than a plugin

The client leg is already written, and it is host-agnostic except for one gate:

- `codexSocket.RoundTrip` (`internal/gateway/codex_socket.go:139`) does the dial, `codexCreate`, header prelude, SSE conversion, kept sockets with `previous_response_id` deltas (`codex_socket_keep.go`), shunning a host that refuses the handshake, `1009` too-big, and `previous_response_not_found` → whole conversation over HTTP.
- The only thing that keeps a relay out is this (`internal/provider/codex_zstd.go:84`):

  ```go
  func codexTurnURL(u *url.URL) bool {
      base, err := url.Parse(CodexBase)
      return err == nil && u != nil && strings.EqualFold(u.Host, base.Host) && u.Path == base.Path+"/responses"
  }
  ```

  i.e. host must be `chatgpt.com` and path `/backend-api/codex/responses`.
- No scheme handling is needed either: `coder/websocket`'s `Dial` takes `http`/`https` and treats them as `ws`/`wss` (`dial.go:119` in v1.8.14, the version in go.mod), and `codexSocket.socket` already dials `*req.URL` as it stands.

What I would expect the change to be:

1. A provider setting, in the shape the others already have (`codex=`, `compaction=`, `patience=`, `user-agent=`): `socket=auto|on|off` (`on` = a custom Responses provider's streamed turns go on its WebSocket; `off`/absent = today's behaviour).
2. In `codexSocket.RoundTrip`, replace `provider.CodexTurnURL(req.URL)` with "Codex's host, or this provider is `socket=on|auto`", and let the existing `codexShun` map do the rest: under `auto`, a relay that refuses the handshake is spoken HTTP for `codexSocketShun` (10 min) and tried again later — no new fallback ladder.
3. Keep the existing drop-outs: handshake not 101 (401/429/5xx go to HTTP and let HTTP say it as it is), connection limit, socket ending before the first event, `previous_response_not_found` → whole conversation over HTTP.

Roughly 20 lines, and every relay that speaks the Codex socket gets it, not just this one. Under `auto` a relay that does not (today most of them answer `426` to the upgrade) would pay one failed handshake per 10 minutes, which is the same trade `#3449` records for `chatgpt.com`.

## Or a plugin, if you would rather keep core free of it

The docs are clear that "a new model source (vendor), or rewriting a request" is a plugin's job and needs no change here, and a provider plugin *can* own its turn: its `loader().fetch` may return a streaming `Response`, so it can open the `wss://`, send `response.create`, and turn frames into SSE. A community plugin already does that shape (`Bian-Sh/magpie-ws-relay-auth`, linked from #5124).

What a plugin cannot do as well here:

- it is a *different* provider — it cannot switch the transport of the `krill-ai-codex` provider already added (with its key, picked models, catalog, `compaction=native`, masking), so the user re-adds the relay as a plugin provider and all of that moves too;
- its fetch is per request in the Bun host, so socket reuse, the `previous_response_id` delta and the fallback ladder are written again in JS (a socket can be keyed by `X-Magpie-Session`, which plugins may read, so it is possible, just duplicated);
- one more hop per request: base64 `chunk` RPC between gateway and host, where the core socket is in-process Go.

If "not in core" is your call, say so and I will write and publish the plugin instead — I would rather have your preference than a patch you would not take.

## Related

- #5124 — the general ask for WebSocket support on third-party relays (this is one relay's verified details)
- #4058 — socket kept across turns, delta continuation
- #5560 — the bytes a full replay costs
- #3449 — the 426/shun noise on `chatgpt.com`

---

**摘要**（中文）：Krill AI 这个中转已经支持 Codex 的 Responses WebSocket（`wss://api.kbsfdxc.net/codex/v1/responses`，`response.create` 帧进、事件帧出、同一 socket 续 `previous_response_id`），实测可用。magpie 里负责这一段的 `codexSocket` 已经写好了，只被 `provider.CodexTurnURL` 挡在 `chatgpt.com` 之外；建议加一个 `socket=auto|on|off` 的供应商选项放开它，而不是让每个中转都去写插件。插件路线也能做（每个请求自己拿 `fetch` 开 socket），但那是另建一个供应商，现有供应商的 key、模型目录、`compaction=native` 都用不上，还要在 JS 里把保活和续接重写一遍。

issue.title: provider: a per-provider switch for the Responses WebSocket (some upstreams serve the same protocol as ChatGPT)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Ask

Some upstreams — relays and self-hosted gateways — serve the same **Responses WebSocket** that Codex speaks to ChatGPT: one socket that outlives a turn, each turn a text frame (`{"type":"response.create", …Responses body…}`), each event of the reply a frame back, and a next turn as only its new input next to `previous_response_id`.

magpie already speaks it to `chatgpt.com` (`codexSocket`), but a provider cannot turn it on, so those upstreams are stuck on HTTP/SSE.

Proposal: one provider field, in the shape the others already have (`codex=`, `compaction=`, `patience=`, `user-agent=`):

```
magpie provider set <id> socket=auto|on|off
```

`off`/absent = today. `auto` = try the socket, fall back to HTTP when the upstream doesn't take it. `on` = the user says it does; still fall back, but don't shun the host.

## Why this is a small change

The client leg is already written and is host-agnostic except for one gate:

- `codexSocket.RoundTrip` (`internal/gateway/codex_socket.go:139`): dials `*req.URL` as it stands (`coder/websocket`'s `Dial` takes `https` and treats it as `wss`, `dial.go:119`), builds `response.create`, reads the prelude headers, converts frames to SSE, keeps a socket per conversation and sends the next turn as a delta after `previous_response_id` (`codex_socket_keep.go`), shuns a host whose handshake is refused, handles `1009` too-big and the connection limit, and falls back to the whole conversation over HTTP on `previous_response_not_found`.
- Only this keeps other hosts out (`internal/provider/codex_zstd.go:84`):

  ```go
  func codexTurnURL(u *url.URL) bool {
      base, err := url.Parse(CodexBase)
      return err == nil && u != nil && strings.EqualFold(u.Host, base.Host) && u.Path == base.Path+"/responses"
  }
  ```

- The one non-trivial bit: the gate lives in a shared `RoundTripper` that never learns which provider a request is for (`upstreamTransport()` in `internal/gateway/upstream_transport.go`), so the flag has to be resolved to a host set — a small registry a provider adds its host to when `socket` is on/auto, and removes it from when it is off.

## What "it works" was checked against

Against one upstream that serves it (handshake and frames only, nothing else in it is special):

- handshake `101` in ~250 ms; `OpenAI-Beta: responses_websockets=2026-02-06` is not enforced by it (101 with or without);
- a turn came back as 10–17 frames, one per SSE event, first `response.output_text.delta` at 2.2–2.5 s;
- the socket stayed `OPEN` after `response.completed`; 100 s idle, then a turn with only its new input and `previous_response_id` answered in context (`cached_tokens: 3968`);
- `service_tier`, `client_metadata`, `prompt_cache_key`, `reasoning.effort`, `store: false` were all accepted.

## Rule I'd expect

- Same fallback ladder as `chatgpt.com`: a handshake that isn't 101 (4xx), a socket that ends before the first event, a connection limit — the turn goes over HTTP; `auto` also adds the host to `codexShun` for 10 minutes (the trade #3449 already documents for `chatgpt.com`), `on` doesn't.
- Nothing above the transport changes: routing groups, keys, fallbacks, usage, masking, `patience`.


## This was asked once before, and the "not now" was about the other leg

#1005 (2026-10-06) asked for exactly this and was closed in a day: "Responses over WebSocket 的转发近期不做", because magpie's *routing, failover, a key's model/account limits, concurrency and usage are all built around one HTTP request* — i.e. a socket the **agent** opens into magpie, which the gateway would then have to account for per turn.

That reasoning does not cover the leg this asks about. Since then the upstream leg was written anyway: magpie → ChatGPT goes over the socket (v0.1.2119, from #4058), and a conversation's next turn goes on the kept socket as a delta (2026-11-07). Nothing the earlier answer worried about came back with it: the agent still speaks HTTP to magpie, so routing, limits, concurrency and usage are judged per request exactly as before — the socket is only how that request reaches the vendor.

So this is not a new accounting model for WebSockets, just the switch that says which providers are reached that way.

Same request as #5124, with the code path and what the upstream actually does; #4058 is the related "keep the socket across turns" work, #5560 the bytes a full replay costs.

---

**摘要**：有些上游的 Responses 接口同时支持 Codex 对 ChatGPT 说的那套 WebSocket 协议（一帧 `response.create` 进、一帧一事件出、socket 跨轮存活、可 `previous_response_id` 只发增量）。magpie 里这段客户端逻辑 `codexSocket` 已经写好了，只是被 `provider.CodexTurnURL()` 固定在 `chatgpt.com`。建议给供应商加一个 `socket=auto|on|off` 字段放开它：`auto` 试用并在握手被拒后 shun 10 分钟退回 HTTP，`on` 仍然回退但不 shun。除这一个开关外不需要新的回退逻辑。
